chapter_text:
CHAPTER 17 — स्वस्तिपन्थामनुचरेम (SVASTIPANTHAMANUCHAREMA)

Introduction — स्वस्ति किम्?

The word स्वस्ति (svasti) is one of the oldest and most auspicious words in the Sanskrit language. It is formed from सु (su = well, good) + अस्ति (asti = it is / may it be), and so it means literally 'may it be well', 'well-being', 'auspiciousness', 'blessing'. A verse or utterance that prays for such well-being is called a स्वस्तिवचन (svasti-vachana, benediction) or मङ्गलमन्त्र (auspicious mantra). The chapter title स्वस्तिपन्थामनुचरेम (svasti panthaam anucharema) comes from the Vedic prayer 'स्वस्ति पन्थामनुचरेम' — 'may we tread the path of well-being'. पन्थाम् means 'the path/road' and अनुचरेम means 'may we follow/walk along'. The whole line is a wish that all of us may walk safely along the auspicious road of life, harming none and blessed by all.

In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we read a small garland of famous public-domain Vedic benedictions and शान्ति-मन्त्र (peace mantras). For each we learn the word meanings (शब्दार्थ), an English translation, and the message; then we tie them together around a single great ideal — सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः, 'may all beings be happy' — and finally draw a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्) from the verses.

Why benedictions matter (स्वस्तिवचनानां महत्त्वम्)

At the beginning and the end of study, worship and every good undertaking, the Sanskrit tradition places a स्वस्तिवचन or a शान्ति-पाठ (peace recitation). These verses are not requests for one person's private gain; they pray for the welfare of ALL — सर्वे (all), समस्ताः लोकाः (all the worlds), प्रजाः (the creatures/people). The heart of the tradition is that true well-being cannot be selfish: my happiness is bound up with the happiness of others, and peace within is bound up with peace in the world around me. To recite these mantras is to train the mind to wish good to everyone and to fear harm to none (मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत् — may no one be a sharer of sorrow). Because they are short, rhythmic and often chanted, they are easy to memorise, and while learning them a student naturally absorbs vocabulary, सन्धि, विभक्ति and verb forms.

Five famous benedictions (शब्दार्थ सहित)

1) सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः ।
   सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: सर्वे = all; भवन्तु = may (they) be; सुखिनः = happy (ones); सन्तु = may (they) be; निरामयाः = free from disease/affliction; भद्राणि = auspicious things, good; पश्यन्तु = may (they) see/experience; मा = not (with wish); कश्चित् = anyone; दुःखभाग् = a sharer of sorrow; भवेत् = may (one) be.
   Translation: May all be happy; may all be free from disease; may all see (experience) what is auspicious; may no one be a sharer of sorrow.
   Message: This is the best-loved of all Sanskrit benedictions. It asks for four blessings for EVERYONE without exception — happiness, health, good fortune and freedom from grief. It is the very definition of universal welfare (लोककल्याण).

2) ॐ सह नाववतु । सह नौ भुनक्तु । सह वीर्यं करवावहै ।
   तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॥ ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: सह = together; नौ = us two; अवतु = may (He/It) protect; भुनक्तु = may (He/It) nourish; वीर्यम् = vigour, strength; करवावहै = may we two do/perform; तेजस्वि = brilliant, full of vigour; अधीतम् = what has been studied, learning; अस्तु = may it be; मा विद्विषावहै = may we two not hate each other.
   Translation: May (the Lord) protect us both (teacher and pupil) together; may He nourish us both together; may we both work together with vigour; may our study be brilliant and effective; may we never hate each other. Om, peace, peace, peace.
   Message: This is the शान्ति-मन्त्र recited by teacher and student before study. It prays for cooperative, harmonious learning free of jealousy and hatred — a beautiful ideal of education as a shared, friendly effort.

3) स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः परिपालयन्तां न्यायेन मार्गेण महीं महीशाः ।
   गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः शुभमस्तु नित्यं लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु ॥
   शब्दार्थ: स्वस्ति = well-being, blessing; प्रजाभ्यः = for the people/creatures; परिपालयन्ताम् = may (they) protect/govern; न्यायेन मार्गेण = by the just path, righteously; महीम् = the earth; महीशाः = kings (lords of the earth); शुभम् = good, welfare; अस्तु = may it be; नित्यम् = always; लोकाः समस्ताः = all the worlds/people; सुखिनः = happy; भवन्तु = may (they) be.
   Translation: May there be well-being for all creatures; may kings protect the earth righteously, by the just path; may there always be welfare for cattle and the learned; and may all the worlds (all people) be happy.
   Message: This great मङ्गलमन्त्र widens the circle of blessing to the whole society — the common people, just rulers, animals, scholars, indeed all the worlds. Its closing line, 'लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु', is one of the most quoted prayers for universal happiness.

4) सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम् ।
   देवा भागं यथा पूर्वे संजानाना उपासते ॥
   शब्दार्थ: सङ्गच्छध्वम् = move/go together; संवदध्वम् = speak together (in one voice); सम् = together; वः = your; मनांसि = minds; जानताम् = let (them) know/be of one accord; देवाः = the gods; भागम् = the share (of offering); यथा = as; पूर्वे = the ancients/former ones; संजानानाः = being of one mind; उपासते = worship/partake.
   Translation: Walk together, speak together; let your minds be of one accord — just as the gods of old, being united in mind, shared their portion together.
   Message: This famous verse from the closing hymn of the Rigveda (the संवाद-सूक्त) is a prayer for unity, cooperation and harmony. It teaches that a people who move together, speak together and think together will prosper — a timeless message for family, school and nation.

5) ॐ द्यौः शान्तिरन्तरिक्षं शान्तिः पृथिवी शान्तिरापः शान्तिरोषधयः शान्तिः ।
   वनस्पतयः शान्तिर्विश्वेदेवाः शान्तिर्ब्रह्म शान्तिः सर्वं शान्तिः शान्तिरेव शान्तिः सा मा शान्तिरेधि ॥
   शब्दार्थ: द्यौः = the heavens/sky; शान्तिः = peace; अन्तरिक्षम् = the mid-region, space; पृथिवी = the earth; आपः = the waters; ओषधयः = the herbs/plants; वनस्पतयः = the trees; विश्वेदेवाः = all the gods; ब्रह्म = the Absolute; सर्वम् = everything; एव = indeed; सा = that (peace); मा = to me; एधि = be! (may it come).
   Translation: May there be peace in the heavens, peace in the mid-region, peace on the earth, peace in the waters; peace among the herbs, peace among the trees; peace among all the gods; peace in Brahman; may everything be peace, only peace; and may that peace come to me.
   Message: This great शान्ति-मन्त्र of the Yajurveda spreads peace outward through every level of creation — sky, space, earth, water, plants, trees, gods, the Absolute — and then asks that the same all-pervading peace flow into oneself. Peace is prayed for the whole cosmos, not for one person alone.

How the verses fit together — the path of well-being (कल्याण-मार्गः)

Read together, these five benedictions describe a single road, the स्वस्ति-पन्थाः, the auspicious path we are invited to walk. सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः sets the goal: the happiness and health of ALL. सह नाववतु shows how learning and friendship should be — cooperative, without hatred. स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः extends the blessing to the whole of society and its just governance. सङ्गच्छध्वम् gives the method — moving, speaking and thinking together in unity. And the शान्ति-मन्त्र द्यौः शान्तिः crowns them all by praying peace for the entire universe and for oneself. The tone throughout is not preachy but hopeful: a wish, a benediction, a prayer that the whole world may be well. To 'tread the path of well-being' (स्वस्ति पन्थामनुचरेम) is to make these wishes the habit of one's own heart.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the mantras

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — joining of sounds).
  • सह नौ अवतु → सह नाववतु. Here नौ + अवतु gives नाव् + अवतु = नाववतु. When the diphthong औ is followed by a vowel it changes to आव् (this is अयादि-सन्धि). Similarly नौ + अधीतम् → नावधीतम् (in तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु).
  • शुभम् + अस्तु → शुभमस्तु (म् simply joins the following vowel). Split back as शुभम् + अस्तु.
  • शान्तिः + एव → शान्तिरेव. A visarga ः after अ/आ, before a soft sound, becomes र् — विसर्ग-सन्धि.
  • सत् + गमय → सद्गमय (the hard त् before the soft ग् softens to द् — व्यञ्जन-सन्धि). This is seen in the well-known line असतो मा सद्गमय.
  • सुखिनः + भवन्तु → सुखिनो भवन्तु. A visarga after उ/अ before a soft consonant becomes ओ (उकार/ओकार विसर्ग-सन्धि).
  Being able to SPLIT a joined form (सन्धि-विच्छेद), e.g. नाववतु = नौ + अवतु, is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role. Examples from the mantras:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, the subject/predicate): सर्वे (all), लोकाः (worlds), महीशाः (kings), सुखिनः (happy) — the ones about whom the wish is made.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, the object): महीम् 'the EARTH' (महीं...परिपालयन्ताम् — 'may they protect the earth'), भागम् 'the share'.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): न्यायेन मार्गेण 'BY the just path'; सह वीर्यम् 'with vigour'.
  • चतुर्थी (dative, 'for/to'): प्रजाभ्यः 'FOR the people', गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः 'FOR cattle and the learned' — the beneficiaries of the blessing.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/at'): implied in द्यौः/अन्तरिक्षम्/पृथिवी as the realms 'in which' peace is prayed.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension — worked example). The a-stem masculine noun लोक (world) declines in the प्रथमा (nominative): एकवचन लोकः (one world), द्विवचन लोकौ (two worlds), बहुवचन लोकाः (many worlds). In the mantra लोकाः समस्ताः the plural लोकाः is the प्रथमा बहुवचन, 'all the worlds'. Compare देव: प्रथमा एकवचन देवः, बहुवचन देवाः (as in विश्वेदेवाः).

(D) धातुरूप (verb forms). Several verbs here are in the लोट् लकार (imperative / benedictive, 'may... / let...') and the विधिलिङ् (potential). Take the धातु भू (to be/become):
  • लोट् लकार, प्रथम पुरुष: भवतु (let one be), भवताम् (let two be), भवन्तु (let many be). सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः uses भवन्तु — 'may all BE happy'.
  • विधिलिङ्, प्रथम पुरुष एकवचन: भवेत् (one might/should be). मा...भवेत् — 'may no one BE (a sharer of sorrow)'.
  From the धातु अस् (to be): लोट् प्रथम पुरुष अस्तु (let it be), सन्तु (let many be) — शुभम् अस्तु, सर्वे सन्तु; and the मध्यम पुरुष एकवचन एधि (be thou!) — शान्तिरेधि. Verbs like पश्यन्तु (from दृश्, 'may they see'), परिपालयन्ताम् ('may they protect') and अवतु ('may He protect') are all imperatives expressing a wish or blessing.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that स्वस्ति means 'well-being / auspiciousness' (सु + अस्ति), that a स्वस्तिवचन or मङ्गलमन्त्र is a benediction praying for such well-being, and that the chapter title स्वस्तिपन्थामनुचरेम means 'may we tread the path of well-being'. You read five famous public-domain Vedic benedictions and शान्ति-मन्त्र: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः (universal happiness and health), सह नाववतु (harmonious teacher-pupil learning), स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः (welfare of all society and just rule), सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम् (unity and cooperation), and द्यौः शान्तिः (peace for the whole cosmos). For each you studied the शब्दार्थ, an English translation and the message; you saw how together they map a single 'path of well-being' whose goal is the welfare of all beings. Finally you drew grammar from the mantras: सन्धि (with सन्धि-विच्छेद), the विभक्ति case endings, a शब्दरूप model (लोकः / लोकौ / लोकाः), and धातुरूप of भू and अस् in the imperative and potential. Memorise a few of these mantras — they will enrich both your Sanskrit and your wish for the good of all.

topics.name: स्वस्ति and स्वस्तिवचन — Benedictions and Universal Welfare
topics.description: What स्वस्ति (सु + अस्ति, 'well-being') and a स्वस्तिवचन / मङ्गलमन्त्र are; the chapter title स्वस्तिपन्थामनुचरेम ('may we tread the path of well-being'); and the central ideal that true well-being is the welfare of all (सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः).

topics.name: शान्ति-मन्त्र — Vedic Peace Invocations
topics.description: The शान्ति-मन्त्र of the tradition — सह नाववतु and द्यौः शान्तिः — how peace (शान्ति) is prayed for teacher and pupil, and outward through every level of creation from sky and earth to the herbs, trees, gods and oneself.

topics.name: The Auspicious Path — स्वस्ति पन्थाः and Selected Mantras
topics.description: The five benedictions read in this lesson (सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः, सह नाववतु, स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः, सङ्गच्छध्वम्, द्यौः शान्तिः), how to read and recite them, and how together they describe a single 'path of well-being'.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building Sanskrit vocabulary through word-by-word शब्दार्थ of each mantra: सुखिनः, निरामयाः, भद्राणि, अवतु, विद्विषावहै, प्रजाभ्यः, न्यायेन, मनांसि, शान्तिः and their English meanings.

topics.name: Values and Ethical Themes — Welfare, Harmony and Peace
topics.description: The values carried by the mantras — universal welfare (लोककल्याण), health and happiness of all, cooperative learning, non-hatred (मा विद्विषावहै), unity and cooperation (सङ्गच्छध्वम्), just governance, and all-round peace (शान्ति).

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Mantras
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the mantras: सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद (e.g. नाववतु = नौ + अवतु), the विभक्ति case endings, a शब्दरूप model of the a-stem noun लोक, and धातुरूप of भू / अस् in the imperative (लोट्) and potential (विधिलिङ्).

branches.label: अर्थः — Meaning & Importance
details: Title: 'may we tread the path of well-being'
Goal: welfare of ALL (सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः)

sections.heading: What स्वस्ति and benedictions are, and why they matter
bullets: स्वस्ति = सु (well/good) + अस्ति (it is / may it be): 'well-being, auspiciousness, blessing'.
A स्वस्तिवचन / मङ्गलमन्त्र is a benediction; a शान्ति-मन्त्र is a peace invocation — both open and close study, worship and every good undertaking.
These verses never pray for private gain alone; they pray for the welfare of ALL (सर्वे, समस्ताः लोकाः, प्रजाः).
The chapter title स्वस्तिपन्थामनुचरेम means 'may we tread the path of well-being'.

sections.heading: Benedictions of universal welfare
bullets: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः...: may all be happy, all free from disease, all see good, and may no one suffer sorrow — the definition of लोककल्याण (universal welfare).
स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः...: may there be welfare for the people, just rule by kings, welfare for cattle and scholars, and 'लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु' — may all the worlds be happy.
सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम्...: walk together, speak together, think together — a Rigvedic prayer for unity and cooperation.

sections.heading: The peace mantras (शान्ति-मन्त्र)
bullets: ॐ सह नाववतु...: a teacher-pupil prayer — may He protect and nourish us both, may we work with vigour, may our study be brilliant, मा विद्विषावहै (may we not hate each other).
ॐ द्यौः शान्तिः...: peace in the heavens, space, earth, waters, herbs, trees, gods and Brahman — peace for the whole cosmos, and 'may that peace come to me'.
शान्तिः is chanted three times (शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः) for peace on every plane.

sections.heading: Sandhi from the mantras
bullets: अयादि-सन्धि: नौ + अवतु = नाववतु (औ → आव् before a vowel); नौ + अधीतम् = नावधीतम्.
विसर्ग-सन्धि: शान्तिः + एव = शान्तिरेव (ः → र्); सुखिनः + भवन्तु = सुखिनो भवन्तु (ः → ओ).
व्यञ्जन-सन्धि: सत् + गमय = सद्गमय (त् → द् before ग्); शुभम् + अस्तु = शुभमस्तु.
सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting a joined form back into its parts) is a key reading skill: नाववतु = नौ + अवतु.

sections.heading: Vibhakti, shabda-rupa and dhatu-rupa
bullets: प्रथमा (subject): सर्वे, लोकाः, महीशाः, सुखिनः; द्वितीया (object): महीम्, भागम्.
तृतीया 'by' न्यायेन मार्गेण; चतुर्थी 'for' प्रजाभ्यः, गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः.
शब्दरूप of a-stem लोक (प्रथमा): एकवचन लोकः, द्विवचन लोकौ, बहुवचन लोकाः.
धातुरूप: भू लोट् भवतु/भवताम्/भवन्तु, विधिलिङ् भवेत्; अस् लोट् अस्तु/सन्तु and मध्यम पुरुष एधि (be thou!).

key_takeaways: स्वस्ति (सु + अस्ति) means 'well-being / auspiciousness'; a स्वस्तिवचन is a benediction, and the title means 'may we tread the path of well-being'.
The supreme ideal of these mantras is universal welfare — सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः, सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः, and मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत्.
सह नाववतु is the teacher-pupil शान्ति-मन्त्र praying for cooperative, harmonious learning: मा विद्विषावहै — may we not hate each other.
स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः widens the blessing to all society and just rule, ending 'लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु'.
सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम् is a Rigvedic prayer for unity and cooperation; द्यौः शान्तिः prays peace for the whole cosmos and for oneself.
अयादि-सन्धि: नौ + अवतु = नाववतु; visarga-sandhi: शान्तिः + एव = शान्तिरेव; splitting a form is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
भवन्तु / सन्तु / अस्तु / एधि are imperative (लोट्) 'may... / let...' forms of भू and अस्; भवेत् is the potential (विधिलिङ्).

glossary.definition: Well-being, auspiciousness, blessing; from सु (well) + अस्ति (it is / may it be).
A benediction; an auspicious utterance or verse (मङ्गलमन्त्र) praying for well-being at the start of a good undertaking.
Peace; the central word of a शान्ति-मन्त्र, chanted three times for peace on every plane.
A peace invocation, e.g. सह नाववतु or द्यौः शान्तिः, recited to invoke peace before and after study or worship.
A path or road; in स्वस्ति पन्थामनुचरेम, the auspicious 'path of well-being' we are to tread.
Free from disease or affliction; healthy — 'सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः', may all be free from disease.
Auspicious, good, blessed; भद्राणि = auspicious things, as in 'सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु'.
People, subjects, creatures; प्रजाभ्यः = 'for the people' (चतुर्थी), the beneficiaries of the blessing.
'May we two not hate each other' — the closing wish of the सह नाववतु शान्ति-मन्त्र, an ideal of non-hatred.
Universal welfare, the good of all the worlds; the aim of 'लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु'.
'Move/go together' — the Rigvedic call to unity in the verse सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम्.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; e.g. अयादि-सन्धि नौ + अवतु = नाववतु.
The splitting of a sandhi form back into its separate words, e.g. नाववतु = नौ + अवतु.
The imperative/benedictive mood expressing a wish or command ('may... / let...'), e.g. भवन्तु, सन्तु, अस्तु, एधि.
The potential mood ('should / might / may'), e.g. भवेत् in 'मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत्'.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — स्वस्तिपन्थामनुचरेम (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 17)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the mantras in the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate the following benediction into simple English:
सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः ।
सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत् ॥
questions.answer: May all be happy (सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः); may all be free from disease (सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः); may all see/experience what is auspicious (सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु); and may no one be a sharer of sorrow (मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत्). It is a prayer for the happiness, health and good fortune of everyone.
questions.explanation: The verse asks four blessings — happiness, health, good fortune and freedom from grief — for all beings without exception.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: सुखिनः, निरामयाः, भद्राणि, पश्यन्तु, दुःखभाग्.
questions.answer: सुखिनः = happy (ones); निरामयाः = free from disease/affliction; भद्राणि = auspicious things, good; पश्यन्तु = may (they) see/experience; दुःखभाग् = a sharer of sorrow.
questions.explanation: These words all come from the mantra सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the message of the शान्ति-मन्त्र 'ॐ सह नाववतु ... मा विद्विषावहै'.
questions.answer: It is the prayer of teacher and pupil before study: may the Lord protect and nourish us both, may we work together with vigour, may our study be brilliant, and may we never hate each other (मा विद्विषावहै). Its message is that learning should be a cooperative, harmonious effort free of jealousy.
questions.explanation: The mantra sets the ideal of shared, friendly learning and non-hatred.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) नाववतु (b) शान्तिरेव.
questions.answer: (a) नाववतु = नौ + अवतु (औ → आव्, अयादि-सन्धि). (b) शान्तिरेव = शान्तिः + एव (visarga ः → र्, विसर्ग-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each word: प्रजाभ्यः, न्यायेन, महीम्.
questions.answer: प्रजाभ्यः = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'for the people'. न्यायेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by/through justice'. महीम् = द्वितीया (accusative) → 'the earth' (the object protected).
questions.explanation: चतुर्थी shows the beneficiary, तृतीया the means, द्वितीया the object.

questions.question: Explain the ideal of universal welfare using the mantra 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः ... मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत्'. How can a student practise this ideal today?
questions.answer:
The mantra prays four blessings for EVERYONE, not for oneself alone: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः (may all be happy), सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः (may all be healthy), सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु (may all see good), and मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत् (may no one suffer). This is लोककल्याण — the ideal that my well-being is bound up with the well-being of all, and that true happiness cannot be selfish.
A student can practise it by wishing well to classmates rather than competing selfishly, helping the sick and the weak, sharing and cooperating, protecting animals and the environment, and thinking of the welfare of all — the school, the community, the world — and not only of 'me and mine'. Reciting the mantra daily trains the heart to fear harm to none and to wish good to everyone.
questions.explanation: Explain the four blessings and the concept of लोककल्याण, then give practical applications.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) that pray for welfare or peace. Give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. सर्वे जनाः सुखिनः भवन्तु। (May all people be happy.)
2. सर्वत्र शान्तिः भवतु। (May there be peace everywhere.)
3. वयं सह पठाम। (May we study together.)
Together these express the chapter's ideal: happiness for all, peace everywhere, and cooperative effort.
questions.explanation: Simple imperative/benedictive sentences using vocabulary from the chapter (भवन्तु, भवतु, पठाम).

questions.question: Translate: 'सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम्' and state its message.
questions.answer: Translation: Walk/move together (सङ्गच्छध्वम्), speak together (संवदध्वम्), let your minds (वः मनांसि) be of one accord (सं...जानताम्). Message: It is a Rigvedic prayer for unity and cooperation — a people who move, speak and think together will prosper.
questions.explanation: The verse teaches harmony of action, speech and mind.

questions.question: In the mantra 'ॐ द्यौः शान्तिः...', why is शान्तिः (peace) prayed for so many things, and what is asked at the very end?
questions.answer: Peace is prayed for the heavens, mid-space, earth, waters, herbs, trees, all the gods and Brahman — that is, for every level of creation — because true peace must pervade the whole cosmos, not one person alone. At the very end it asks 'सा मा शान्तिरेधि' — may that (all-pervading) peace come to me as well.
questions.explanation: Peace is invoked outward through creation, then drawn back into oneself.

questions.question: What is a स्वस्तिवचन, and give two reasons why such benedictions are valued in the Sanskrit tradition.
questions.answer: A स्वस्तिवचन is a benediction — an auspicious verse or utterance (from स्वस्ति = सु + अस्ति, 'well-being') that prays for the welfare of all at the start of study, worship or any good undertaking. Two reasons it is valued: (1) it trains the mind to wish good to everyone and harm to none (universal welfare); (2) being short and often chanted, it is easy to memorise and helps a learner absorb vocabulary and grammar.
questions.explanation: Definition (स्वस्ति = सु + अस्ति) plus its moral and educational value.

questions.explanation: प्रजाभ्यः = 'for the people' — the beneficiary.

questions.question: In 'न्यायेन मार्गेण', both words are in the
questions.explanation: 'By the just path' — the means, so instrumental.

questions.question: In 'महीं...परिपालयन्ताम्', the word महीम् is in the
questions.explanation: The earth is the object protected — accusative.

questions.question: 'भवन्तु' (as in सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः) is which लकार of the धातु भू?
questions.explanation: भवन्तु = 'let/may (they) be' — imperative, प्रथम पुरुष बहुवचन.

questions.question: 'सन्तु' (सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः) is a form of which धातु?
questions.explanation: सन्तु = 'let (them) be', लोट् प्रथम पुरुष बहुवचन of अस्.

questions.question: 'भवेत्' (मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत्) is in which mood?
questions.explanation: भवेत् = 'might/should be', विधिलिङ् प्रथम पुरुष एकवचन.

questions.question: The शब्दरूप (nominative plural) of the a-stem noun लोक is
questions.explanation: प्रथमा: एकवचन लोकः, द्विवचन लोकौ, बहुवचन लोकाः.

questions.question: 'एधि' (शान्तिरेधि) is the imperative (लोट्) of which धातु, in the 2nd person singular?
questions.explanation: एधि = 'be thou!', मध्यम पुरुष एकवचन लोट् of अस्.

questions.question: The best translation of 'सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः' is
options: may all be free from disease
questions.answer: may all be free from disease
questions.explanation: सन्तु = may they be; निरामयाः = free from disease.

questions.question: The best translation of 'सह नौ भुनक्तु' is
options: may He nourish us both together
questions.answer: may He nourish us both together
questions.explanation: सह = together; नौ = us two; भुनक्तु = may He nourish.

questions.question: 'गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः शुभमस्तु' means
options: may there be welfare for cattle and the learned
questions.answer: may there be welfare for cattle and the learned
questions.explanation: गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः = for cattle and brahmins (the learned).

questions.question: The line 'सा मा शान्तिरेधि' (end of द्यौः-शान्तिः) means
options: may that peace come to me
questions.answer: may that peace come to me
questions.explanation: सा (that peace) मा (to me) एधि (be/come) — may that peace be mine.

questions.question: The best translation of 'सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम्' is
questions.explanation: सङ्गच्छध्वम् = move together; संवदध्वम् = speak together.

questions.question: 'स्वस्ति' means misfortune or bad luck.
questions.explanation: स्वस्ति means well-being / auspiciousness, not misfortune.

questions.question: 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः' prays for the happiness of all.
questions.explanation: It wishes happiness for सर्वे (all).

questions.question: 'मा विद्विषावहै' means 'let us hate each other'.
questions.explanation: With मा (not) it means 'may we NOT hate each other'.

questions.question: 'निरामयाः' means 'free from disease'.
questions.explanation: निरामय = without disease, healthy.

questions.question: 'ॐ सह नाववतु' is a शान्ति-मन्त्र recited by teacher and pupil.
questions.explanation: It is the classic teacher-student peace prayer before study.

questions.question: 'शुभम् + अस्तु' joins to form 'शुभमस्तु'.
questions.explanation: म् joins the following vowel: शुभम् + अस्तु = शुभमस्तु.

questions.question: 'शान्तिः' is chanted three times at the end of a शान्ति-मन्त्र.
questions.explanation: ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः — for peace on every plane.

questions.question: 'भवन्तु' is a past-tense (imperfect) verb form.
questions.explanation: भवन्तु is लोट् लकार (imperative), 'may/let (they) be'.

questions.question: The mantra 'सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम्' is about fighting one another.
questions.explanation: It is a prayer for unity and cooperation, not conflict.

questions.question: 'शान्तिः' means peace.
questions.explanation: शान्तिः = peace.

questions.question: सर्वे भवन्तु ____ । (fill the missing word)
questions.explanation: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः — may all be happy.

questions.question: सर्वे सन्तु ____ ।
questions.explanation: सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः — may all be free from disease.

questions.question: सर्वे ____ पश्यन्तु ।
questions.explanation: सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु — may all see auspicious things.

questions.question: मा ____ दुःखभाग्भवेत् ।
questions.explanation: मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत् — may no one suffer sorrow.

questions.question: सह ____ अवतु । (whom does He protect — 'us two'?)
questions.explanation: सह नौ अवतु (joined नाववतु) — may He protect us both.

questions.question: The सह नाववतु mantra ends: मा ____ ।
questions.explanation: मा विद्विषावहै — may we two not hate each other.

questions.question: स्वस्ति ____ परिपालयन्तां न्यायेन मार्गेण महीं महीशाः ।
questions.explanation: स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः — well-being for the people.

questions.question: लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो ____ ।
questions.explanation: लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु — may all the worlds be happy.

questions.question: सङ्गच्छध्वं ____ सं वो मनांसि जानताम् ।
questions.explanation: सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वम् — walk together, speak together.

questions.question: ॐ द्यौः ____ अन्तरिक्षं शान्तिः ।
questions.explanation: ॐ द्यौः शान्तिः अन्तरिक्षं शान्तिः — peace in sky and space.

questions.question: Give the one-word English meaning of 'शान्तिः': ____.
questions.explanation: शान्तिः = peace.

questions.question: Give the one-word English meaning of 'मही': ____.
questions.explanation: मही = the earth.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: नाववतु = नौ + ____ .
questions.explanation: नाववतु splits back into नौ + अवतु (अयादि-सन्धि).

questions.question: 'भवन्तु' is a form of the धातु ____ (root meaning 'to be/become').
questions.explanation: भवन्तु is the लोट् (imperative) प्र.पु. बहुवचन of भू.

questions.question: Give the one-word English meaning of 'सुखिनः': ____.
questions.explanation: सुखिनः = happy (ones).

questions.question: Translate into English: 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः'.
questions.answer: May all be happy; may all be free from disease. It prays that everyone enjoy both happiness (सुखिनः) and health (निरामयाः).
questions.explanation: सर्वे = all; भवन्तु/सन्तु = may they be; सुखिनः = happy; निरामयाः = free from disease.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'ॐ सह नाववतु। सह नौ भुनक्तु।'
questions.answer: Om. May He protect us both together; may He nourish us both together. It is the opening of the teacher-pupil peace prayer.
questions.explanation: सह = together; नौ = us two; अवतु = may protect; भुनक्तु = may nourish.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the mantra 'स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः परिपालयन्तां न्यायेन मार्गेण महीं महीशाः। गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः शुभमस्तु नित्यं लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु॥'.
questions.answer: May there be well-being for all creatures (स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः); may kings (महीशाः) protect the earth (महीम्) righteously, by the just path (न्यायेन मार्गेण); may there always be welfare (शुभम् अस्तु नित्यम्) for cattle and the learned (गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः); and may all the worlds/people (लोकाः समस्ताः) be happy. The mantra widens the blessing from ordinary people to just rulers, animals, scholars and finally the whole world.
questions.explanation: It is a great मङ्गलमन्त्र praying for welfare across all of society and for just governance.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: निरामयाः, भद्राणि, दुःखभाग्, पश्यन्तु.
questions.answer: निरामयाः = free from disease; भद्राणि = auspicious things / good; दुःखभाग् = a sharer of sorrow; पश्यन्तु = may (they) see/experience.
questions.explanation: All four come from the mantra सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः.

questions.question: What value does the phrase 'मा विद्विषावहै' teach, and where does it occur?
questions.answer: It teaches non-hatred and harmony. It occurs at the end of the सह नाववतु शान्ति-मन्त्र, where teacher and pupil pray 'may we never hate each other', so that learning remains a friendly, cooperative effort free of jealousy.
questions.explanation: मा (not) + विद्विषावहै (may we two hate) = may we not hate each other.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) नाववतु (b) शुभमस्तु.
questions.answer: (a) नाववतु = नौ + अवतु (अयादि-सन्धि, औ → आव्). (b) शुभमस्तु = शुभम् + अस्तु (म् joins the following vowel).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and role of each: प्रजाभ्यः, न्यायेन, महीम्.
questions.answer: प्रजाभ्यः = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'for the people' (beneficiary). न्यायेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by/through justice' (means). महीम् = द्वितीया (accusative) → 'the earth' (object protected).
questions.explanation: चतुर्थी shows the beneficiary, तृतीया the means, द्वितीया the object.

questions.question: Identify the धातु and verb-form (लकार/mood) of: भवन्तु, सन्तु, भवेत्.
questions.answer: भवन्तु = धातु भू, लोट् लकार (imperative), प्रथम पुरुष बहुवचन ('may they be'). सन्तु = धातु अस्, लोट् लकार, प्रथम पुरुष बहुवचन ('let them be'). भवेत् = धातु भू, विधिलिङ् (potential), प्रथम पुरुष एकवचन ('might/should be').
questions.explanation: लोट् expresses a wish/command; विधिलिङ् expresses possibility/should.

questions.question: What is a शान्ति-मन्त्र, and give one example from this chapter.
questions.answer: A शान्ति-मन्त्र is a peace invocation recited to invoke peace before and after study or worship, ending with 'शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः'. An example from this chapter is 'ॐ सह नाववतु...' (or 'ॐ द्यौः शान्तिः...').
questions.explanation: शान्ति = peace; the mantra prays for peace on every plane.

questions.question: Explain the meaning and message of 'सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम्'.
questions.answer: It means: walk/move together, speak together, and let your minds be of one accord. Its message is unity and cooperation — a people who act, speak and think together in harmony will prosper.
questions.explanation: A Rigvedic prayer for harmony of deed, word and thought.

questions.question: How does the mantra 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः...' express the ideal of universal welfare (लोककल्याण)?
questions.answer: It asks four blessings for EVERYONE, not for oneself: happiness (सुखिनः), freedom from disease (निरामयाः), the seeing of good (भद्राणि पश्यन्तु), and that no one suffer sorrow (मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत्). By repeating सर्वे ('all'), it makes the welfare of all beings its only goal — the essence of लोककल्याण.
questions.explanation: The word सर्वे and the four blessings together define universal welfare.

questions.question: Translate 'मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत्' and say what it wishes.
questions.answer: Translation: May no one be a sharer of sorrow. It wishes that no living being should ever have to suffer grief.
questions.explanation: मा = not; कश्चित् = anyone; दुःखभाग् = sharer of sorrow; भवेत् = may be.

questions.question: In the द्यौः-शान्तिः mantra, name three of the realms for which peace is prayed and state what is asked at the end.
questions.answer: Peace is prayed for many realms, e.g. द्यौः (the heavens), पृथिवी (the earth) and आपः (the waters) — also space, herbs, trees and the gods. At the end it asks 'सा मा शान्तिरेधि' — may that (all-pervading) peace come to me.
questions.explanation: Peace is invoked outward through creation and then drawn into oneself.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: प्रजाभ्यः, महीशाः, न्यायेन, समस्ताः.
questions.answer: प्रजाभ्यः = for the people/creatures; महीशाः = kings (lords of the earth); न्यायेन = by justice; समस्ताः = all/entire.
questions.explanation: All four come from the स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः mantra.

questions.question: Write out the full mantra that begins 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः'.
questions.answer: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः। सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत्॥
questions.explanation: The complete two-line benediction for universal welfare.

questions.question: Join by सन्धि: (a) सह + नौ + अवतु (b) शान्तिः + एव.
questions.answer: (a) सह नौ अवतु → सह नाववतु (नौ + अवतु = नाववतु, अयादि-सन्धि). (b) शान्तिः + एव → शान्तिरेव (visarga ः → र्, विसर्ग-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Applying sandhi joins separate words into the recited forms.

questions.question: What value about education does the सह नाववतु mantra express?
questions.answer: It expresses that education should be a cooperative, harmonious effort between teacher and pupil — both protected and nourished together, working with shared vigour, their study made brilliant, and above all free of hatred and jealousy (मा विद्विषावहै).
questions.explanation: Learning is pictured as a shared, friendly, respectful partnership.

questions.question: Translate 'न्यायेन मार्गेण महीं महीशाः परिपालयन्ताम्'.
questions.answer: May the kings (महीशाः) protect/govern the earth (महीम्) by the just, righteous path (न्यायेन मार्गेण). It prays for just and righteous governance.
questions.explanation: The mantra asks rulers to rule fairly, not by force.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of the a-stem noun लोक in the प्रथमा (nominative), all three numbers.
questions.answer: एकवचन लोकः, द्विवचन लोकौ, बहुवचन लोकाः. In the mantra 'लोकाः समस्ताः' the plural लोकाः ('all the worlds') is प्रथमा बहुवचन.
questions.explanation: The a-stem masculine नोun declines रामः-fashion: लोकः / लोकौ / लोकाः.

questions.question: Explain the word स्वस्ति and say why benedictions (स्वस्तिवचन) open and close good undertakings.
questions.answer: स्वस्ति is formed from सु (well/good) + अस्ति (it is / may it be), and means 'well-being, auspiciousness, blessing'. A स्वस्तिवचन (benediction) opens and closes study, worship and every good undertaking because the tradition holds that a good work should begin and end with a wish for the welfare of ALL, not for private gain. Such prayers train the mind to wish good to everyone and harm to none, and being short and chanted they are easy to remember.
questions.explanation: Definition (सु + अस्ति) plus the reason benedictions frame good actions.

questions.question: Why does the द्यौः-शान्तिः mantra invoke peace at so many levels (sky, earth, waters, herbs, trees, gods)?
questions.answer: Because true peace cannot belong to one person or one place alone; it must pervade the whole of creation. By naming every level — from the heavens down to the herbs and trees, and up to the gods and Brahman — the mantra prays that peace fill the entire cosmos, and only then asks that the same peace flow into oneself.
questions.explanation: The spreading imagery shows peace as universal and all-pervading.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: वीर्यम्, तेजस्वि, अधीतम्, विद्विषावहै.
questions.answer: वीर्यम् = vigour/strength; तेजस्वि = brilliant/full of vigour; अधीतम् = what has been studied (learning); विद्विषावहै = may we two hate (used with मा = 'may we not hate').
questions.explanation: All four come from the सह नाववतु mantra.

questions.question: Discuss the ideal of universal welfare in the mantra 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः...' and explain how it can guide our conduct today.
questions.answer:
The mantra prays four blessings for everyone without exception: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः (may all be happy), सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः (may all be healthy), सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु (may all experience good), and मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग् भवेत् (may no one suffer sorrow). The repeated word सर्वे makes clear that its concern is लोककल्याण — the welfare of all beings — and its logic is that my happiness is not separate from the happiness of others.
Today this ideal can guide conduct in many ways: wishing well to others rather than competing selfishly; helping the sick, the poor and the weak; being kind across differences of nation, religion or background; caring for animals and the environment; and working for the good of the community and the world. It also shapes the heart inwardly — one who daily prays that no one suffer learns compassion and loses cruelty. Thus the mantra is not merely words but a training of the will toward the welfare of all.
questions.explanation: State the four blessings and the concept of लोककल्याण, then give concrete modern applications.

questions.question: Write four simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) that pray for welfare, peace or unity, and give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. सर्वे जनाः सुखिनः भवन्तु। (May all people be happy.)
2. सर्वत्र शान्तिः भवतु। (May there be peace everywhere.)
3. वयं सह पठाम सह वर्धामहै। (May we study and grow together.)
4. मा कोऽपि दुःखी भवतु। (May no one be sorrowful.)
Together these echo the chapter's ideals of universal happiness, peace, cooperation and freedom from sorrow.
questions.explanation: Simple benedictive sentences using imperative forms (भवन्तु, भवतु, पठाम) and chapter vocabulary.

questions.question: Explain the सह नाववतु शान्ति-मन्त्र line by line, giving the word meanings and its overall message.
questions.answer:
सह नाववतु (सह नौ अवतु) = 'may He protect us both together' — teacher and pupil are protected as one. सह नौ भुनक्तु = 'may He nourish us both together' — both are sustained together. सह वीर्यं करवावहै = 'may we both work together with vigour (वीर्यम्)' — study is a joint, energetic effort. तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु (नौ अधीतम् अस्तु) = 'may what we study be brilliant and effective (तेजस्वि)'. मा विद्विषावहै = 'may we never hate each other'. It closes with ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः.
Message: This is the peace prayer of teacher and student before study. It pictures education as a shared partnership in which both are protected, nourished and energised together, their learning made bright, and — most beautifully — bound by friendship rather than jealousy or hatred. It is an ideal of cooperative, harmonious learning.
questions.explanation: Explain each clause with word meanings, then summarise the ideal of harmonious learning.

questions.question: Using 'सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम्', explain the value of unity and cooperation and how it can be practised in a school.
questions.answer:
The verse calls people to move together (सङ्गच्छध्वम्), speak together (संवदध्वम्) and be of one mind (सं वो मनांसि जानताम्) — that is, to unite in action, speech and thought, just as the gods of old shared their portion by being of one mind. Its value is that unity and cooperation bring strength and prosperity, while division brings weakness.
In a school this can be practised by working together on projects, listening to and speaking with one another respectfully, resolving quarrels by agreement, helping weaker classmates, and pursuing common goals such as cleanliness or a class function as a team rather than as rivals. When students move, speak and think together in harmony, the whole class flourishes — exactly what the mantra prays for.
questions.explanation: Explain the threefold unity (deed, word, thought) and give practical school applications.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि with three examples taken from the mantras of this chapter, showing the join and the split.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; splitting a joined form back is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
1. अयादि-सन्धि: नौ + अवतु = नाववतु — the diphthong औ before a vowel becomes आव्. Split: नाववतु = नौ + अवतु.
2. विसर्ग-सन्धि: शान्तिः + एव = शान्तिरेव — the visarga ः before a soft sound becomes र्. Split: शान्तिरेव = शान्तिः + एव. Similarly सुखिनः + भवन्तु = सुखिनो भवन्तु (ः → ओ).
3. व्यञ्जन/स्वर join: शुभम् + अस्तु = शुभमस्तु — म् joins the following vowel. Split: शुभमस्तु = शुभम् + अस्तु.
Being able to both join and split these forms is essential for reading and reciting the mantras correctly.
questions.explanation: Give the rule and three worked join/split pairs drawn from the mantras.

questions.question: Explain विभक्ति and धातुरूप using examples from the mantras of this chapter.
questions.answer:
विभक्ति (case endings) show a word's role. From the mantras: प्रथमा (subject) सर्वे, लोकाः, महीशाः; द्वितीया (object) महीम्; तृतीया (by) न्यायेन मार्गेण; चतुर्थी (for) प्रजाभ्यः, गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः. A shabdarupa model is the a-stem लोक: प्रथमा लोकः / लोकौ / लोकाः.
धातुरूप (verb forms): most verbs here are in the लोट् लकार (imperative, 'may/let'). From भू: भवतु / भवताम् / भवन्तु (सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः). From अस्: अस्तु, सन्तु (शुभम् अस्तु; सर्वे सन्तु), and मध्यम पुरुष एधि 'be thou!' (शान्तिरेधि). भवेत् (मा...भवेत्) is विधिलिङ् (potential), 'might/should be'. Verbs like पश्यन्तु, परिपालयन्ताम् and अवतु are also imperatives expressing a wish or blessing.
questions.explanation: Cover the main cases with examples and the imperative/potential verb forms of भू and अस्.

questions.question: Explain the idea of स्वस्ति-वचन and शान्ति-मन्त्र in the Sanskrit tradition and why they matter.
questions.answer:
A स्वस्ति-वचन is a benediction — an auspicious verse or utterance (from स्वस्ति = सु + अस्ति, 'well-being') that prays for welfare. A शान्ति-मन्त्र is a peace invocation ending in 'शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः'. The tradition places such prayers at the beginning and end of study, worship and every good work.
They matter for three reasons. First, they are selfless: they pray for सर्वे (all) and समस्ताः लोकाः (all the worlds), not for private gain, and so train the heart in compassion and universal welfare. Second, they set the right frame of mind — peace, humility and goodwill — before an important task. Third, being short and rhythmic, they are easy to memorise, and while learning them a student naturally absorbs vocabulary, सन्धि, विभक्ति and verb forms. Thus स्वस्ति-वचन and शान्ति-मन्त्र are at once moral, spiritual and educational.
questions.explanation: Define both, then give the selfless, mind-framing and educational reasons they are valued.

questions.question: Explain the द्यौः-शान्तिः mantra and the idea of threefold peace (शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः).
questions.answer:
The Yajurveda mantra 'ॐ द्यौः शान्तिः...' prays peace for the heavens (द्यौः), the mid-region (अन्तरिक्षम्), the earth (पृथिवी), the waters (आपः), the herbs (ओषधयः), the trees (वनस्पतयः), all the gods (विश्वेदेवाः), Brahman (ब्रह्म) and everything (सर्वम्) — and ends 'सा मा शान्तिरेधि', 'may that peace come to me'. Peace is thus spread through every level of creation and then drawn into oneself.
The threefold chant 'शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः' is traditionally understood as a prayer for peace from the three kinds of trouble — those arising from the higher powers/fate (आधिदैविक), from other beings and surroundings (आधिभौतिक), and from oneself, body and mind (आध्यात्मिक). Chanting peace three times therefore asks for complete, all-round peace, outer and inner.
questions.explanation: Describe the spreading imagery of peace and the traditional threefold (आधिदैविक/आधिभौतिक/आध्यात्मिक) meaning.

questions.question: Read the verse and answer: 'सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः। सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत्॥' — Translate the verse into simple English.
questions.answer: May all be happy; may all be free from disease; may all see (experience) what is auspicious; and may no one be a sharer of sorrow. It is a benediction praying for the happiness, health and good fortune of everyone.
questions.explanation: सर्वे = all; सुखिनः = happy; निरामयाः = free from disease; भद्राणि = good; मा कश्चित्...भवेत् = may no one be.

questions.question: Read: 'ॐ सह नाववतु। सह नौ भुनक्तु। सह वीर्यं करवावहै। तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै॥' — Who recite this mantra, and what do they pray for?
questions.answer: Teacher and pupil recite it together before study. They pray that God protect and nourish them both, that they work together with vigour, that their study become brilliant and effective, and — above all — that they never hate each other (मा विद्विषावहै). It is a prayer for cooperative, harmonious learning.
questions.explanation: The mantra is the classic guru-shishya peace prayer for shared, friendly study.

questions.question: Read: 'स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः परिपालयन्तां न्यायेन मार्गेण महीं महीशाः। गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः शुभमस्तु नित्यं लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु॥' — Which values about society and governance does this mantra convey?
questions.answer: It conveys several values: (1) concern for the welfare of the common people (स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः); (2) just and righteous governance — kings should protect the earth 'न्यायेन मार्गेण', by the just path, not by force; (3) care for animals and scholars/the learned (गोब्राह्मणेभ्यः शुभमस्तु); and (4) universal welfare — 'लोकाः समस्ताः सुखिनो भवन्तु', may all the worlds be happy. Together they picture a just, compassionate society caring for all its members.
questions.explanation: The mantra links good governance with the welfare of every section of society.

questions.question: Read: 'सङ्गच्छध्वं संवदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम्।' — Give the meaning of सङ्गच्छध्वम्, संवदध्वम् and मनांसि.
questions.answer: सङ्गच्छध्वम् = move/go together; संवदध्वम् = speak together (in one voice); मनांसि = minds. The line asks people to act, speak and think together in unity.
questions.explanation: The three words carry the ideas of united action, speech and thought.

questions.question: Read: 'ॐ सह नाववतु' — the word नाववतु is a sandhi form. Do its सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi.
questions.answer: नाववतु = नौ + अवतु. It is अयादि-सन्धि: the diphthong औ, when followed by a vowel, changes to आव् (नौ → नाव् before अवतु).
questions.explanation: ए/ऐ/ओ/औ before a vowel become अय्/आय्/अव्/आव् — the अयादि-सन्धि rule.

questions.question: Read: 'स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः ... न्यायेन मार्गेण महीं महीशाः।' — State the विभक्ति (case) of प्रजाभ्यः and of महीम्.
questions.answer: प्रजाभ्यः is in the चतुर्थी विभक्ति (dative, 'for the people') — the beneficiary of the blessing. महीम् is in the द्वितीया विभक्ति (accusative, 'the earth') — the object that the kings protect.
questions.explanation: चतुर्थी marks the beneficiary; द्वितीया marks the object of परिपालयन्ताम्.

questions.question: Read: 'स्वस्ति पन्थामनुचरेम' (may we tread the path of well-being) — What does the word स्वस्ति mean, and what kind of utterance is this?
questions.answer: स्वस्ति means 'well-being, auspiciousness, blessing' (from सु + अस्ति). This line is a स्वस्ति-वचन (benediction) — an auspicious prayer that we may all walk safely along the path of well-being.
questions.explanation: स्वस्ति = well-being; the line is a benediction, the source of the chapter title.

questions.question: Read: 'ॐ द्यौः शान्तिरन्तरिक्षं शान्तिः पृथिवी शान्तिः ... शान्तिरेव शान्तिः सा मा शान्तिरेधि॥' — Explain what this mantra prays for and what 'सा मा शान्तिरेधि' means.
questions.answer: The mantra prays for peace (शान्तिः) at every level of creation — the heavens, the mid-region, the earth, the waters, the herbs, the trees, all the gods and Brahman — so that peace pervades the entire cosmos. 'सा मा शान्तिरेधि' means 'may that (all-pervading) peace come to me' — after spreading peace through all the worlds, the reciter asks that the same peace flow into his or her own self.
questions.explanation: Peace is invoked outward through creation and then drawn inward to oneself.

questions.question: Read: 'तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै।' — What value does 'मा विद्विषावहै' teach, and why is it important between teacher and pupil?
questions.answer: 'मा विद्विषावहै' means 'may we two not hate each other', and it teaches the value of non-hatred and mutual goodwill. It is important between teacher and pupil because learning flourishes only in an atmosphere of trust and friendship; jealousy or hatred would spoil the shared effort of study.
questions.explanation: Non-hatred keeps the teacher-pupil relationship cooperative and fruitful.

questions.question: Read: 'मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत्।' — Translate this line and identify the word that means 'anyone'.
questions.answer: Translation: 'May no one be a sharer of sorrow.' The word meaning 'anyone' is कश्चित् (with मा making it 'no one'); दुःखभाग् = sharer of sorrow, भवेत् = may be.
questions.explanation: मा + कश्चित् = 'may no one'; the line wishes that none should suffer grief.
